severity: none - documented behaviour within stated numerical tolerance

found_by: cforge-fuzz Qiskit campaign, N1 amplitude oracle, seed 777
expected: cp(theta) = diag(1,1,1,e^{i*theta}); exact decomposition uses 2 CX
observed: at optimization_level 2 and 3, cp(theta) for |theta| below sqrt(2)e-4 is synthesized as two rz gates with zero CX. Levels 0 and 1 keep both CX exactly. Process infidelity at theta=9.623e-05 is 5.788e-10. Independent of approximation_degree (same result for 1.0 and None).
reproducer_python:
import numpy as np
from qiskit import QuantumCircuit, transpile
from qiskit.quantum_info import Operator
qc = QuantumCircuit(2); qc.cp(9.623e-05, 0, 1)
t = transpile(qc, basis_gates=['rz','sx','x','cx'], optimization_level=3, approximation_degree=1.0)
print([i.operation.name for i in t.data])   # ['rz','rz'] — no cx
notes: CORRECTIONS to the original entry, both found on re-measurement 2026-09-15:
(1) it fires at optimization_level 2 as well, not only 3;
(2) the error is 5.8e-10 process infidelity, not the 2.4e-5 quoted. That figure was an N1 amplitude distance, a different metric, and quoting it here overstated the finding.

DECISION: not reported. The original entry made reporting conditional on the Qiskit maintainers showing interest in edge cases on entry 001. They confirmed and fixed #16594, which is not the same thing. The condition was never met.
Kept in the zoo as a negative result. A campaign that only records what it reports is not an honest record of what it found.
